entities.summary:
Sicardus of Cremona (1155–1215) was an Italian prelate, historian and writer.

As a key figure in the medieval Italian Church, Sicardus played a significant role in shaping the theological and liturgical landscape of his time.

He was a prolific writer and historian, best known for his chronicle of the Lombard Kingdom, which provides valuable insights into the politics, society and culture of medieval Italy.

Sicardus's work had a lasting impact on the development of medieval historiography and the study of the Lombard Kingdom, making him one of the most important figures in the history of Italian historiography.

Despite his significant contributions, Sicardus's work has been largely overshadowed by that of his contemporaries, and it was not until the 20th century that his chronicle was rediscovered and recognized as a major historical source.

The rediscovery of Sicardus's chronicle in the 20th century has been credited with a new era of Italian historiography, as scholars have sought to reclaim and reevaluate the contributions of medieval Italian historians like Sicardus.

In conclusion, Sicardus of Cremona's work has left a lasting legacy in the fields of medieval historiography and Italian studies, demonstrating the enduring importance of his chronicle in shaping our understanding of medieval Italy.
